Navos 2.0 Brings Multi-Agent Commerce, Workato Ships 60+ MCP Servers, KPMG: 75% Expect Enterprise Agents Within a Year

Navos 2.0 brings multi-agent agentic commerce. Workato ships 60+ MCP servers. Brand governance enters AI workflows.

  1. 1

    Tec-Do Launches Navos 2.0: Multi-Agent "Agentic Commerce" at WAIC

    At the 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference, Tec-Do unveiled Navos 2.0 — a multi-agent AI platform that coordinates specialized agents for product selection, creative generation, and influencer outreach through unified workflows. Built on their proprietary marketing LLM "Tec-Chi" (ranked #1 on SuperCLUE-Mkt), it's a clear signal that agentic marketing is moving from concept to coordinated execution.

    Workato Launches Enterprise MCP Registry with 60+ Production Servers

    Workato just shipped the infrastructure layer that enterprise AI has been missing: a governed registry for MCP servers covering CRM, HR, finance, marketing, and 50+ other domains. The key concept: "Enterprise Skills" — pre-built, auditable business capabilities that agents can invoke without hallucinating their way through raw API calls. This is MCP growing up.

  3. 3

    Monotype Brings Brand Governance to AI Workflows via MCP

    Monotype launched an Enterprise MCP Connector (beta) that brings typography licensing and brand governance directly into AI creative tools like Claude and ChatGPT. It checks generated content against approved fonts, returns production-ready CSS, and flags licensing issues before they become problems. Brand governance is now part of the AI workflow, not an afterthought.

    Fireworks AI Raises $1.5B for Multi-Model Enterprise Agents

    Fireworks AI closed a massive $1.5B Series D to expand its multi-model AI platform for enterprise agentic workloads. The funding signals where enterprise AI investment is heading: not single-model bets, but infrastructure that orchestrates multiple models for demanding production scenarios. The agentic enterprise needs serious plumbing.

    KPMG: 75% Expect Enterprise AI Agents Within a Year

    KPMG's 2026 Global Tech Report shows enterprises integrating AI agents into daily operations at scale, with nearly three-quarters expecting enterprise-level deployment within 12 months. The shift from pilot to production is accelerating — and the governance gap is widening just as fast. Read this one: The Workato MCP Registry announcement. MCP is becoming the enterprise standard for AI-to-system connectivity, but raw protocol access isn't enough. What matters is governed, auditable, reusable business capabilities that any agent can invoke safely. "Enterprise Skills" is exactly the abstraction layer that's been missing. Watch this space — it's how agentic AI scales without chaos.
